Survey Q1, 'How frequently do you come to this park?' - coded in questionnaire order: 1 = 6 or 7 days a week, 2 = 2 to 5 days a week, 3 = 1 day a week, 4 = 1 to 3 days a month, 5 = less than one day a month (so higher = less frequent).

Survey Q9, 'About how many different species of flowering plants would you say are here?' - 5-point banded guess (values are band floors: <5, 6-10, 11-20, 21-30, >30).

Actual number of flowering-plant species recorded at the site via the source study's 1m x 1m quadrat transect surveys (Pett 2018 thesis, Sec 4.3.3); range 1-31 matches the thesis's reported site range exactly. Not the respondent's guess (see PlantGuess).
Survey Q10, 'About how many of the species of plants in this area do you think are native to the UK?' - 5-point banded guess (0/25/50/75/100 = none/quarter/half/three-quarters/all).

Actual percentage of native flowering species at the site, classified via the Online Atlas of the British & Irish Flora from the same quadrat surveys as plrich (Pett 2018 thesis, Sec 4.3.3). Not the respondent's guess (see NativeGuess).
Survey Q11, 'About how colourful would you say this area is?' - 5-point scale, 1 = very few colours to 5 = very many colours.
Survey Q12, 'Do you think this area provides useful resources for pollinating insects?' - 5-point scale, 1 = poor/not useful to 5 = excellent/very useful.

Survey question 'What is your gender?' with tickboxes Male / Female. Resolved: filtering to Task == 1 and cross-tabulating Gender x city reproduces the same cell counts as the thesis's sample-composition table (Pett 2018, Table S5.7.2), confirming 0 = Female, 1 = Male (Leeds 121 F / 95 M; Bristol 77 / 75; Edinburgh 107 / 88).
Ordinal age-band code (1-6); AgeLevel gives the corresponding band floor in years.
Age-band floor in years; six bands 18-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65+ (Pett 2018 thesis, p.88), one-to-one with age.
Highest qualification, 6 categories from 'no qualifications' to 'degree/higher degree/NVQ4-5/professional qualifications'.
Employment status, 5 categories: employed / unemployed and looking / not working (e.g. full-time parent) / retired / in full-time education.

Mean score on the (state-version) Connectedness to Nature Scale (Mayer et al. 2009), adapted by the source study: 7-point scale, 1 = strongly disagree to 7 = strongly agree, averaged across scale items (Pett 2018 thesis, Ch.4). -999 is the missing/not-completed flag.
Survey Q15, 'In the last five years have you been a member of any wildlife conservation or natural heritage organisation (e.g. RSPB, Wildlife Trust, National Trust)?' - Yes/No.

Same as CNS_ScaleMean, but without the -999 flag. Not constructed by any script in this repo (present already in the raw Anonymised.csv - data received pre-cleaned, see README). Study team clarifies the pipeline's general convention for -999 is listwise deletion, not value replacement (e.g. script 01 drops rows with missing AgeLevel/non-positive Income/Education rather than imputing them) - so despite the '_MeanUpdated' name this is unlikely to be a mean-imputed version of CNS_ScaleMean; more likely a corrected re-scoring done upstream by the original depositor.
